seo.title: Everest Base Camp Heli Tour — 14 Days | Adventure Access
seo.description: Fourteen days from Kathmandu: Lukla, Namche Bazaar, Kala Pathar at sunset and Everest Base Camp, then a helicopter back from Pheriche. From $3,100.

hero.title: Everest Base Camp
hero.subtitle: The classic trek from Lukla to Base Camp and Kala Pathar, with a helicopter back to Kathmandu
hero.imageAlt: A hiker with arms spread above a sea of clouds and snow peaks

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: More Than Reaching Base Camp
paragraphs: This is one of the classic routes in Nepal, and it offers far more than the arrival at Everest Base Camp. The trek runs from Lukla up the Khumbu Valley through Namche Bazaar, Dingboche and Lobuche to Kala Pathar and Base Camp, then down to Pheriche.

From Pheriche, we arrange a helicopter back to Kathmandu. It saves the long walk down to Lukla and gets you back to the city sooner. Our guides meet you at the airport in Kathmandu and handle the details from there.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Slowly, Slowly
dayTypes.lede: That is the mantra for trekking up the Khumbu. We move at a calculated pace so we do not burn you out early or rush acclimatization. Each trekking day we leave after breakfast, stop for lunch on the trail, and arrive mid-afternoon to rest.

cards.title: City days
cards.body: Days 1–2 and 13–14: arrival, a cultural tour in Boudha, orientation for the trek, and a free day at the end.

cards.title: Trekking days
cards.body: Days 3–11: an average of 4–6 hours on the trail, with longer days of 6–9 hours for Kala Pathar and Base Camp.

cards.title: Acclimatization days
cards.body: Days 5 and 8: climb high, sleep low. A hike to Khumjung from Namche Bazaar, and a steep round-trip climb to the Nagarjun viewpoint from Dingboche.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: Up the Khumbu, Back by Air
chapters.lede: Trek times and sleeping altitudes are approximate.

groups.title: Kathmandu — Getting Ready

image.alt: The eyes of Boudhanath stupa under prayer flags

prose: From the moment you meet your guide at the airport, you are in good hands. No need to find your hotel in the back alleys of Boudha or Thamel on your own. There is still plenty of time to explore, eat well, get to know your guide and prepare for the mountains.

days.label: Day 1
days.text: Arrive in Kathmandu, meet your guide and transfer to your hotel.

days.label: Day 2
days.text: A cultural tour in Boudha, the trek orientation, and dinner with your guide and group.

groups.overnight: 2 Nights · Kathmandu, usually a 3-star hotel in Boudha

groups.title: Lukla to Namche Bazaar — Into the Khumbu

image.alt: The Lukla runway seen from under a canopy

prose: Lukla is one of the most thrilling airport locations in the world. It sits on a mountainside among Himalayan peaks, and no roads reach it: you fly or you walk. Yak caravans come right to the door to carry supplies toward Namche Bazaar and beyond.

days.label: Day 3
days.text: Fly to Lukla, stop for tea, then a 3–4 hour starter trek down the valley to Phakding at 8,659 ft. Food is provided; pack water and sunscreen.

days.label: Day 4
days.text: About 6–7 hours to Namche Bazaar at 11,316 ft, including the first steep switchbacks of the valley.

days.label: Day 5
days.text: The first acclimatization hike, to Khumjung village and back to Namche. On clear days, your first views of Ama Dablam and Everest.

groups.overnight: 1 Night · Phakding, then 2 Nights · Namche Bazaar

groups.title: Deboche, Dingboche and Lobuche — Above the Tree Line

image.alt: A decorated yak on the trail

prose: After Namche Bazaar the serious work begins. The trail leaves the forests behind and climbs well above the tree line, and the land starts to look like the Himalaya you imagined.

days.label: Day 6
days.text: About 5–6 hours to Deboche. Sleep at about 12,660 ft.

days.label: Day 7
days.text: About 6–7 hours to Dingboche. Sleep at about 14,497 ft.

days.label: Day 8
days.text: Acclimatization day: a steep round-trip hike, close to a climb, to the Nagarjun viewpoint.

days.label: Day 9
days.text: About 4–5 hours to Lobuche. Sleep at about 16,104 ft.

groups.title: Kala Pathar and Everest Base Camp

image.alt: Signposts for Kala Pathar and Everest Base Camp

prose: From Base Camp, Everest is barely visible because the surrounding peaks block the view. So we climb Kala Pathar first, to catch the evening light on Everest's slopes. The next day, Base Camp puts you on the Khumbu Glacier with time to explore part of the site.

days.label: Day 10
days.text: Trek to Kala Pathar for a sunset view of Everest, then back to Gorak Shep for the night. About 8–9 hours. Sleep at about 16,990 ft.

days.label: Day 11
days.text: Trek to Everest Base Camp, then down the valley to Pheriche. About 6–7 hours of walking. Sleep at about 13,841 ft.

groups.title: Pheriche to Kathmandu — By Helicopter

image.alt: A red helicopter flying past snowy mountains

prose: The helicopter shortens the trek by two full days and gives a more reliable departure from the region. On clear days, the mountains go by your window all the way back to Kathmandu.

days.label: Day 12
days.text: Fly by helicopter from Pheriche to Kathmandu, with aerial views of the Himalaya.

days.label: Day 13
days.text: A free day in Kathmandu: rest, revisit favorite places from the start of the trip, and repack.

days.label: Day 14
days.text: Your guide picks you up at the hotel and takes you to the airport for your flight.

groups.overnight: 2 Nights · Kathmandu, usually a 4-star hotel in Thamel

pullQuote: Slowly, slowly. This is the mantra for trekking up the Khumbu Valley.

highlights.title: Sunset from Kala Pathar
highlights.body: The climb to 18,433 feet for evening light on the slopes of Everest, a view Base Camp cannot give you.
highlights.imageAlt: A decorated yak on the trail

highlights.body: A steep round-trip acclimatization climb from Dingboche, then back to sleep at the same altitude.

highlights.title: The Flight In
highlights.body: A mountainside airstrip with no road access, among Himalayan peaks, where yak caravans load supplies right at the door.

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Kathmandu
cards.body: Your guide meets you at the airport and takes care of the details, so you can take in the city. Your time there includes good food, getting to know your guide, and an orientation for the trek.

cards.title: Pace
cards.body: Itineraries are built around an average of 4–6 hours of trekking a day. Expect several steep switchbacks, starting on the climb to Namche Bazaar.

cards.title: Altitude
cards.body: Climb high, sleep low. On acclimatization days we hike higher, often to viewpoints of peaks like Everest and Ama Dablam, then return to sleep at the same altitude. This reduces the risk of altitude sickness.

cards.title: The flight out
cards.body: A helicopter from Pheriche to Kathmandu saves two days of walking down to Lukla and gives a more reliable departure from the region.

cards.title: Alcohol
cards.body: We strongly encourage little or no alcohol while acclimatizing. If you do drink when appropriate, you settle your tab at the close of the meal.

stays.label: Where You'll Stay
stays.heading: Kathmandu Hotels
paragraphs: Hotels from 3 to 5 stars are available in Kathmandu. We generally choose a 3-star hotel in Boudha at the start of the trip and a 4-star hotel in Thamel at the end, and confirm the choice with you when you book.
